justification: Adds a gate over what reports ASSERT, and changes three report surfaces plus the pre-push policy. The conveyancing fix changes what a paid PDF says when a spatial query fails, which is a behaviour change to customer-facing output; the Sol change can now block a push. Both are cheap to get wrong quietly.

falsifiable_check.fails_when: A report surface asserts a site verdict with no interpolation and no branch that could change it. Anchored to two reference cases run on every change: the PRE-FIX ContextSection.tsx (the real DQ-36 TOD line) must exit 1, and current main must exit 0. The first version of this lint FAILED that anchor — it reported PASSED on the very file DQ-36 came from, because it tested interpolation across a window and a neighbouring line's template literal masked the hardcoded one.

pre_impl.existing_data: 36 files across frontend-nextjs/components/pdf, frontend-nextjs/lib/pdf and the three Python conveyancing modules. Sweep result: 4 findings needing a decision, plus 2 verified false positives now annotated. Scope was bounded deliberately to surfaces a paying customer reads; the rest of the app was NOT swept and is called out as such.
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: Expected the class to be large and concentrated in React. It is neither. Only one live React instance remained after PR 858, and the worst finding was in Python: get_unique_overlays catches every exception and returns an empty result, so a PostGIS outage produced the same empty `flagged` list as a genuinely unconstrained property, and the PDF printed 'No constraints identified for this property'. A clean bill of health from a query that never ran, on the section a conveyancer buys the report for.
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: No existing check inspects whether a rendered verdict is backed by received data. liability_language_check scans wording, lint_hardcoded_zone_codes scans values, validate_schema_contract compares code to catalog, lint_brief_failsoft guards the brief's service layer. The findings-plus-named-escape shape is copied from the zone-code lint rather than invented.

functions.name: scan_file
functions.input: a path to a TypeScript, TSX or Python file in the report surfaces
functions.output: a list of findings, each classified as either FABRICATED or UNDETERMINED with its line and text
functions.if_none: an empty list means no verdict strings matched, which is reported as zero findings rather than as an assertion that the file is clean

functions.name: _window
functions.input: the file's lines, the finding index, and how many lines of context to take
functions.output: the surrounding source text used for the escape-comment search and, with a tighter span, the branch test
functions.if_none: near the top of a file the slice is clamped, so a finding on line one still gets a valid window rather than raising

values: N/A - the lint reads source text, not business values.

queries.purpose: none added; the conveyancing fix only reinterprets the covered_layers value already returned by the existing overlay query
queries.where_clause: no new SQL. get_unique_overlays keeps its existing point/polygon predicates; this change reads its covered_layers return value to tell a completed screen from a failed one

break_it.scenario: The lint cannot detect the very defect it was written for, and ships looking green.
break_it.what_happens: It did exactly that. Version one tested interpolation across a 6-line window, so the Housing SEPP template literal above the TOD line masked it and the pre-fix file reported PASSED.
break_it.how: Interpolation is now tested on the literal only. Both reference cases are asserted in the test suite, so the anchor cannot rot.

break_it.scenario: A PostGIS outage makes a paid conveyancing report state that the property has no constraints.
break_it.what_happens: get_unique_overlays returns ([], set(), {}) on any exception, so flagged was empty and the report printed 'No constraints identified for this property'. Now covered_layers distinguishes a screen that ran from one that did not, and the third state says plainly that it is not a finding of unconstrained.
break_it.how: Three-state branch plus tests asserting the old two-state expression cannot return.

break_it.scenario: The lint is TypeScript-shaped and flags every Python if-guarded verdict, so nobody trusts it.
break_it.what_happens: Four false positives in the conveyancing report on the first Python run, all guarded by `if is_strata:` which the TS-only branch pattern could not see.
break_it.how: Python statement and ternary forms added, with a test that reproduces the strata block shape.

break_it.scenario: The branch window is so wide that any nearby conditional excuses a hardcoded verdict, quietly disarming the gate.
break_it.what_happens: At 14 lines the founding case downgraded from FABRICATED to non-blocking UNDETERMINED. The window was tuned against both reference cases: at 5 the strata blocks still false-positived, at 6 they clear and the founding case still blocks.
break_it.how: Escape comments keep the wide window; the branch test uses the tight one. Both anchors are tested.

break_it.scenario: Someone silences a finding with a bare escape comment and no justification.
break_it.what_happens: The escape pattern required only a non-space character, so `{/* verdict-ok: */}` passed because the closing `*/}` counted as the reason.
break_it.how: The reason must now begin with a letter; a bare escape no longer clears a finding.

break_it.scenario: An absent local-provision fetch renders as a finding that no local provisions apply.
break_it.what_happens: additionalLocalProvisions collapsed 'assessed, none' and 'never assessed' both to undefined, and two components printed a definitive negative. Now undefined means not assessed, empty array means assessed with none.
break_it.how: Blast radius checked before writing: the only other consumer, seeBuilders, uses `?? []`, so an empty array is a no-op there.
break_it.repro: grep -n 'Not assessed - local provision data unavailable' frontend-nextjs/components/pdf/ContextSection.tsx

break_it.scenario: Sol blocks on everything, one finding in three is wrong, and people start pushing with --no-verify.
break_it.what_happens: Blocking is scoped to HIGH severity AND a diff touching served or printed output; everything else stays advisory. The block message states the false-positive rate and names the escape.
break_it.how: SOL_OVERRIDE must carry a reason of at least 15 characters, which is echoed into the push output so the justification exists on the record.

break_it.scenario: The lint file lands untracked because scripts/ is whitelist-ignored, so the gate exists on one machine only.
break_it.what_happens: Explicit whitelist entry added and tracking confirmed rather than assumed.
break_it.how: git ls-files --error-unmatch on the new script before commit.

post_merge.db_reset: None. No schema or data change; the conveyancing fix only reinterprets an existing return value.
post_merge.secrets: None new. Sol blocking uses the OpenAI key already required by the advisory step; with no key the review is skipped and the push proceeds.
post_merge.manual_verify: Generate a conveyancing report with the database unreachable and confirm the callout reads 'Constraint screening did not complete' rather than 'No constraints identified'. Then push a change under frontend-nextjs/components/pdf with a deliberate HIGH-severity defect and confirm the push is blocked and names the SOL_OVERRIDE escape.
